claim: Rough-legged buzzards move southwest and then back northeast as the snowline advances.

claim: The continuous movement of Rough-legged buzzards makes their wintering range dynamic throughout the season.

claim: Rough-legged buzzards started their fall migration on 28 September (mean ± sd for the day of the year: 271 ± 11, n = 31).

claim: The second part of the slow phase was 54 ± 7 days shorter than the first (p<0.001).

claim: The migration speed was 104 ± 6 km/day during the quick phase and 12 ± 7 km/day during the slow phase, that is, about eight times higher (p<0.001).

claim: There was no significant difference between the migration distances of male and female Rough-legged buzzards.

source: During quick phases, Rough-legged buzzards crossed the forest zone, while during the slow phase, they migrated within the grassland and cropland zones (Figure 2).

claim: The study tracked 43 adult Rough-legged buzzards (35 females and 8 males) with solar GPS-GSM loggers.

claim: The taiga zone proved to be an unfavorable habitat during the quick phase of foxtrot migration.
